chapter: Chicago, Ohio and Jelly Roll Morton
title: Arriving in New York, 1928, and the Virginia clique in Jelly's band
summary: Thomas recalls arriving through the tunnel, his first subway ride, Jelly meeting him in Harlem, and the band wondering who the new little alto was.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: That was about 1928 or '29. I think it was about '28. I think it was about '28, because later I got with the Missourians. I remember I came in by way of... I think I came in on the Erie. Because I know I caught the train in New Jersey, and had to take the tunnel to...
I remember you telling me that before.
I took the tunnel through. And I got... I had never seen in a subway in my life. So I got on the
subway, and Jelly met me at the 135th Street station. So he lived on 38th or 37th Street, somewhere in there...
Yeah, that's where all them houses, beautiful houses were.
I got the impression that the guys in the band was wondering, 'Who is this little cat coming in here to play with us?' See, half the guys in the band were from Virginia, because Lester Ward and...
Lester Ward! That name Lester, then Ward...
Ward Pinkett and Joe Garland... I don't remember if Procope was from where or not. But I know there was a kind of...
There was a little clique. But I could tell they wanted to know what I could do. But I could read. I remember reading them orchestrations, that was...
